```{r}
# =====================================================================
# DataJam 2026 - Step 1: Clean and analyze listings.csv.gz
# Data: Inside Airbnb, Vancouver, 15 June 2026, CC BY 4.0
#
# HOW TO USE
#   1. Put listings.csv.gz in a folder called data/
#   2. Run this script top to bottom (Ctrl+Shift+Enter in RStudio)
#   3. Read the printed output: those numbers feed your decision log
#   4. Charts and tables are saved to outputs/
# =====================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)

dir.create("outputs", showWarnings = FALSE)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. SETTINGS (change these to test alternatives for your decision log)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
MAX_MIN_NIGHTS <- 28     # keep listings with minimum_nights BELOW this
ACTIVE_ONLY    <- TRUE   # TRUE = drop listings with 0 reviews in last 12 months
PRICE_CAP_PCT  <- 0.99   # drop nightly prices above this percentile
MIN_GROUP_N    <- 15     # smallest group size we are willing to report

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. LOAD
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
raw <- read_csv("listings.csv.gz", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  clean_names()

cat("\nRaw rows:", nrow(raw), " Raw columns:", ncol(raw), "\n")

# Make sure the columns we need exist (Inside Airbnb changes them over time)
needed <- c("id", "price", "room_type", "minimum_nights",
            "neighbourhood_cleansed", "bedrooms", "availability_365",
            "estimated_occupancy_l365d", "estimated_revenue_l365d",
            "number_of_reviews_ltm")
missing_cols <- setdiff(needed, names(raw))
if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
  stop("These columns are missing from your file: ",
       paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "),
       "\nRun names(raw) and adjust the script.")
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. CONVERT TEXT COLUMNS TO NUMBERS
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Prices are stored as text like "$1,234.00". parse_number() strips the $ and commas.
df <- raw |>
  mutate(
    price                   = parse_number(as.character(price)),
    estimated_revenue_l365d = parse_number(as.character(estimated_revenue_l365d)),
    has_licence = if ("license" %in% names(raw)) {
      !is.na(license) & trimws(license) != ""
    } else NA
  )

cat("Listings with a missing price:", sum(is.na(df$price)),
    "(", round(100 * mean(is.na(df$price)), 1), "% )\n")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. CLEANING WITH A LOG (every step records rows left and median revenue)
#    The log table is your data-quality evidence AND your decision-log numbers.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
clean_log <- tibble(step = character(), rows = integer(),
                    median_revenue = numeric(), mean_revenue = numeric(),
                    median_price = numeric())

log_step <- function(log, step, data) {
  bind_rows(log, tibble(
    step           = step,
    rows           = nrow(data),
    median_revenue = median(data$estimated_revenue_l365d, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_revenue   = mean(data$estimated_revenue_l365d, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_price   = median(data$price, na.rm = TRUE)
  ))
}

clean_log <- log_step(clean_log, "0. Raw", df)

# Step A: entire homes only (DDD buys whole properties, not rooms)
df <- df |> filter(room_type == "Entire home/apt")
clean_log <- log_step(clean_log, "A. Entire home/apt only", df)

# Step B: short-term stays only (28+ night minimums are mid-term rentals)
df <- df |> filter(minimum_nights < MAX_MIN_NIGHTS)
clean_log <- log_step(clean_log, paste0("B. minimum_nights < ", MAX_MIN_NIGHTS), df)

# Step C: valid price and revenue estimate
df <- df |> filter(!is.na(price), price > 0, !is.na(estimated_revenue_l365d))
clean_log <- log_step(clean_log, "C. Valid price and revenue", df)

# Step D: active listings only (at least 1 review in last 12 months)
if (ACTIVE_ONLY) {
  df <- df |> filter(number_of_reviews_ltm > 0)
  clean_log <- log_step(clean_log, "D. Active (>=1 review in last 12 months)", df)
}

# Step E: cap extreme nightly prices (luxury outliers and data errors)
price_cap <- quantile(df$price, PRICE_CAP_PCT, na.rm = TRUE)
df <- df |> filter(price <= price_cap)
clean_log <- log_step(clean_log,
                      paste0("E. Price <= ", round(price_cap), " (", PRICE_CAP_PCT * 100, "th pct)"), df)

# Step F: bedroom groups (studios often have NA bedrooms, so we drop unknowns and log it)
df <- df |>
  mutate(bedroom_group = case_when(
    is.na(bedrooms) ~ NA_character_,
    bedrooms <= 1   ~ "Studio/1BR",
    bedrooms == 2   ~ "2BR",
    bedrooms >= 3   ~ "3+BR"
  ),
  bedroom_group = factor(bedroom_group, levels = c("Studio/1BR", "2BR", "3+BR")))
df <- df |> filter(!is.na(bedroom_group))
clean_log <- log_step(clean_log, "F. Known bedroom count", df)

cat("\n===== CLEANING LOG (put this on a slide / in the appendix) =====\n")
print(clean_log |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 0))), n = Inf)
write_csv(clean_log, "outputs/cleaning_log.csv")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. VALIDATION: do two different revenue methods agree?
#    Method 1: Inside Airbnb estimate (based on reviews)
#    Method 2: price x nights marked unavailable on the calendar
#    Method 2 is an UPPER bound because blocked nights count as "booked".
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
df <- df |>
  mutate(rev_calendar = price * (365 - availability_365))

ratio  <- median(df$rev_calendar / pmax(df$estimated_revenue_l365d, 1), na.rm = TRUE)
corr   <- cor(df$rev_calendar, df$estimated_revenue_l365d, use = "complete.obs")

cat("\n===== VALIDATION =====\n")
cat("Median revenue, Inside Airbnb estimate:", round(median(df$estimated_revenue_l365d)), "\n")
cat("Median revenue, calendar method:       ", round(median(df$rev_calendar, na.rm = TRUE)), "\n")
cat("Median ratio (calendar / IA estimate): ", round(ratio, 2), "\n")
cat("Correlation between the two:           ", round(corr, 2), "\n")

p_val <- ggplot(df, aes(estimated_revenue_l365d, rev_calendar)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "red") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::dollar, limits = c(0, 150000)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar, limits = c(0, 150000)) +
  labs(title = "Two revenue methods compared",
       subtitle = "Red line = perfect agreement. Calendar method counts blocked nights as booked.",
       x = "Inside Airbnb estimated annual revenue",
       y = "Price x unavailable nights",
       caption = "Data: Inside Airbnb, Vancouver, 15 June 2026, CC BY 4.0") +
  theme_minimal()
ggsave("outputs/validation_scatter.png", p_val, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 200)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. LICENSED vs ALL LISTINGS (estimate only: the licence field is imperfect)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
if (!all(is.na(df$has_licence))) {
  cat("\n===== LICENCE CHECK (estimate) =====\n")
  cat("Share of clean listings showing any licence text:",
      round(100 * mean(df$has_licence), 0), "%\n")
  lic_tbl <- df |>
    group_by(has_licence) |>
    summarise(n = n(),
              median_revenue = median(estimated_revenue_l365d),
              median_price   = median(price), .groups = "drop")
  print(lic_tbl)
  write_csv(lic_tbl, "outputs/licence_comparison.csv")
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. MAIN ANALYSIS: revenue by neighbourhood and bedroom group
#    p25 / median / p75 give us a range without any advanced statistics.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
summarise_rev <- function(data, ...) {
  data |>
    group_by(...) |>
    summarise(
      n              = n(),
      median_price   = median(price),
      median_occ_pct = median(estimated_occupancy_l365d / 365 * 100, na.rm = TRUE),
      p25_revenue    = quantile(estimated_revenue_l365d, 0.25),
      median_revenue = median(estimated_revenue_l365d),
      p75_revenue    = quantile(estimated_revenue_l365d, 0.75),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    filter(n >= MIN_GROUP_N) |>
    arrange(desc(median_revenue))
}

by_neigh      <- summarise_rev(df, neighbourhood_cleansed)
by_neigh_bed  <- summarise_rev(df, neighbourhood_cleansed, bedroom_group)
by_bed        <- summarise_rev(df, bedroom_group)

cat("\n===== BY BEDROOM GROUP (whole city) =====\n")
print(by_bed)
cat("\n===== TOP 10 NEIGHBOURHOODS BY MEDIAN REVENUE =====\n")
print(head(by_neigh, 10))
cat("\nNeighbourhoods dropped for having fewer than", MIN_GROUP_N, "listings:",
    n_distinct(df$neighbourhood_cleansed) - nrow(by_neigh), "\n")

write_csv(by_neigh,     "outputs/revenue_by_neighbourhood.csv")
write_csv(by_neigh_bed, "outputs/revenue_by_neighbourhood_bedroom.csv")
write_csv(by_bed,       "outputs/revenue_by_bedroom.csv")

# Chart: median revenue by neighbourhood with the p25-p75 range
p_neigh <- by_neigh |>
  slice_head(n = 12) |>
  mutate(neighbourhood_cleansed = fct_reorder(neighbourhood_cleansed, median_revenue)) |>
  ggplot(aes(median_revenue, neighbourhood_cleansed)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = p25_revenue, xmax = p75_revenue)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0("n=", n)), nudge_y = 0.35, size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) +
  labs(title = "Median annual revenue by neighbourhood",
       subtitle = "Dot = median, line = 25th to 75th percentile. Entire homes only.",
       x = "Estimated annual revenue per listing", y = NULL,
       caption = "Data: Inside Airbnb, Vancouver, 15 June 2026, CC BY 4.0") +
  theme_minimal()
ggsave("outputs/revenue_by_neighbourhood.png", p_neigh, width = 8, height = 5.5, dpi = 200)

# Chart: revenue by bedroom group
p_bed <- ggplot(df, aes(bedroom_group, estimated_revenue_l365d)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar, limits = c(0, 150000)) +
  labs(title = "Annual revenue by bedroom group",
       x = NULL, y = "Estimated annual revenue per listing",
       caption = "Data: Inside Airbnb, Vancouver, 15 June 2026, CC BY 4.0") +
  theme_minimal()
ggsave("outputs/revenue_by_bedroom.png", p_bed, width = 6, height = 4.5, dpi = 200)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. SAVE CLEAN DATA for the next script (costs, yield, scenarios)
#    Note: this keeps listing ids, so do NOT show it on slides.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
write_csv(df |> select(id, neighbourhood_cleansed, bedroom_group, accommodates,
                       price, availability_365, estimated_occupancy_l365d,
                       estimated_revenue_l365d, rev_calendar, has_licence),
          "outputs/listings_clean.csv")

cat("\nDone. Check the outputs/ folder.\n")
```
